title: Lid agent communication contract
coordination_model: Lid is the sole router. A specialist receives a minimal assignment packet only from Lid and returns a minimal result packet only to Lid.

notification_protocol.name: OpenSpec
notification_protocol.purpose: Notify Lid of requirements, acceptance criteria, compliance assessments, and correction requests using the scoped common envelope.

field_rules.handoff_id: Unique ID assigned by Lid for this packet.
field_rules.cycle: Integer from 0 to 5; use 0 before corrective work begins.
field_rules.sender: Configured agent ID that produced the handoff.
field_rules.recipient: Always lid for subagent handoffs; Lid names the intended next specialist in next_action.
field_rules.message_type: One of requirement, architecture, implementation, integration, code_review, test_report, compliance_assessment, correction_request, documentation, or unresolved_error_report.
field_rules.status: One of accepted, complete, blocked, failed, needs_correction, or approved.
field_rules.summary: Short result statement, including affected scope.
field_rules.evidence: File paths, test commands/results, requirement IDs, logs, screenshots, or reproducible steps; say not_available when none exists.
field_rules.next_action: Concrete action, owning agent, and acceptance condition.
field_rules.scope_id: Identifier of the authorized ownership scope and task packet.

field_rules.objective: A bounded task statement with no unrelated project history.
field_rules.allowed_paths: Only paths the specialist may read or modify for this assignment.
field_rules.allowed_requirements: Only requirement IDs needed to complete the task.
field_rules.provided_contracts: Only interface, schema, fixture, or result artifacts required at the boundary.
field_rules.acceptance_criteria: Observable completion conditions for this assignment.
field_rules.verification_expectations: Permitted verification evidence or controlled test result required by Lid.

field_rules.changed_artifacts: Only artifacts inside allowed_paths; use an empty array if no file changed.
field_rules.provided_contracts: Stable outputs the next specialist needs, without disclosing unrelated source or history.
field_rules.verification: Commands, results, test evidence, or controlled-run evidence for the assigned scope.
field_rules.blockers: Concrete missing contract or authorization information; do not request broad repository access.

access_policy.least_context: Specialists receive only an assignment packet and the explicitly supplied boundary contracts. Other specialties are black boxes.
access_policy.history_isolation: Lid does not forward another specialist's task history, private reasoning, source tree, or unrelated result packets.
access_policy.communication: Specialists never address another specialist directly and never delegate. Every question, blocker, result, and correction returns to Lid.
access_policy.filesystem: Read, glob, grep, and edit access is denied outside the ownership scope. Unrestricted shell access is denied because it can bypass path boundaries.
access_policy.review: Code review is performed from a Lid-curated read-only review bundle containing only the changed artifacts, applicable requirements, contracts, and verification evidence.

lite.definition: A localized, low-risk change with no data, API, architecture, deployment, or cross-component impact; for example, renaming a frontend button.
lite.completion: Code reviewer reports no blocking findings.

medium.definition: A bounded feature or fix that affects one or more components but does not require a new system architecture or every specialty.
medium.completion: Compliance analyst approves all applicable requirements and quality criteria.

hard.definition: A cross-cutting, high-risk, or architecture-changing task with database, backend, frontend, integration, operational, security, or major quality impact.
hard.completion: Compliance analyst approves all requirements and quality criteria after evidence from every applicable specialist.

cycle_limit.cycle_definition: A routed correction followed by the required code review, system testing, and compliance reassessment.
cycle_limit.on_unresolved_after_limit: Lid asks technical-writer for an unresolved_error_report addressed to the user; it must list unresolved findings, attempted cycles, impact, blockers, and recommended next actions.

communication_rules: Use only the assignment packet, allowed paths, requirement IDs, and boundary contracts supplied by Lid.
Treat every other specialist's implementation, history, and internal decisions as a black box.
Return one structured result packet to Lid when work is complete, blocked, or needs correction.
Never claim completion without evidence relevant to the role.
Report blockers and contract conflicts immediately; do not silently change another agent's scope.
Reference requirement IDs and acceptance criteria in review, test, and compliance findings.
Code-review and compliance findings must be actionable and identify severity, affected scope, evidence, and acceptance condition.
Only Lid may delegate to another subagent, classify a task, or disclose a cross-boundary contract.
Do not inspect, search, modify, or request access to files outside the allowed ownership scope.
